    Summary and Schedule

    Taxonomic and functional profiling of shotgun metagenomics data with nf-core/taxprofiler and nf-core/funcprofiler, and import of the outputs into R with mia.

    Contributors: Claudio Díaz García, Thi Quynh Trang Nguyen

    Prerequisite

    Prerequisites

    • Basic Unix command line
    • Basic R
    • Setup completed before the workshop
    Setup Instructions Download files required for the lesson
    Duration: 00h 00m  1. Shotgun metagenomics data to study the microbiome What is the human gut microbiome and how can we study it with sequencing?
    How does shotgun metagenomics differ from marker-gene (16S rRNA) sequencing?
    What is the difference between taxonomic and functional profiling?
    Which dataset will we use in this workshop, and how do we obtain it?
    Duration: 00h 10m  2. Reproducible workflows with Nextflow and nf-core Why is reproducibility a challenge in bioinformatics?
    What are Nextflow and nf-core, and how do they help?
    How do I connect to a Nectar instance and check that the software is available?
    How do I prepare the input files needed by nf-core/taxprofiler and nf-core/funcprofiler?
    Duration: 00h 20m  3. Taxonomic profiling with nf-core/taxprofiler How do I configure and run nf-core/taxprofiler?
    How do sylph, mOTUs, Kraken2/Bracken and MetaPhlAn differ?
    How do I interpret the pipeline outputs?
    Which table do I need for downstream analysis in R?
    Duration: 01h 30m  4. Functional profiling with nf-core/funcprofiler How do I configure and run nf-core/funcprofiler?
    What do HUMAnN and eggNOG-mapper measure?
    What is the difference between gene-family abundance, pathway abundance and pathway coverage?
    Duration: 01h 40m  5. Importing and exploring microbiome data with R Which R data structures are used for microbiome data?
    How do I import a taxonomic profile, a functional profile and sample metadata into R?
    How do I aggregate, filter and transform microbiome data?
    Duration: 02h 10m  6. Wrap up What did we do today, from FASTQ files to pipeline outputs?
    What comes next?
    Duration: 02h 20m Finish

    The actual schedule may vary slightly depending on the topics and exercises chosen by the instructor.

    You do not need to install or download anything for this workshop. Everything runs on cloud instances on Nectar that the instructors set up for you. You only need a laptop with:

    • an SSH client, to connect to the Nectar instance on the command line. macOS and Linux have one in the Terminal, while on Windows use PowerShell, Windows Terminal or MobaXterm.
    • an up-to-date web browser, to use RStudio Server and open the pipeline reports.

    The instructors will give you the IP addresses, usernames and passwords on the day.

    Computing environments

    Part of the workshop Where it runs How you connect What is pre-installed
    Nextflow and nf-core pipelines (Day 1) Nectar instance SSH, command line Java, Nextflow, Apptainer/Singularity, nf-core/taxprofiler, nf-core/funcprofiler, input data and reference databases
    Analysis in R (Day 1 and Day 2) RStudio Server on Nectar Web browser R, RStudio, all R packages and the pipeline outputs needed for both days

    Connecting to the Nectar instance (command line)

    BASH 

    ssh <username>@<instance-IP>

    Enter the password when prompted. You should now see a prompt on the Nectar instance.

    Connecting to RStudio Server (R)

    1. Open http://<rstudio-IP> in your web browser. The instructors will give you the address.
    2. Log in with your username and password.
    3. To check that everything is available, run in the RStudio console:

    R 

    library(mia)
library(miaViz)
packageVersion("mia")
list.files("/data/workshop_data")

    You should see the mia version and the folders funcprofiler, metadata and taxprofiler.

    Data

    • 5 simulated human gut metagenomes, Illumina paired-end, from Sun, Huang et al. (2021) Challenges in benchmarking metagenomic profilers. Nature Methods 18:618–626. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-021-01141-3
    • Source: figshare project 79916, dataset Gut_sample: https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.12234947.v1
    • 10 FASTQ files (Gut_sampleN.left.fq.gz and Gut_sampleN.right.fq.gz) and 2 ground-truth tables (5_gut_taxonomic_abd.txt, 5_gut_sequence_abd.txt)

    On the workshop instances:

    • the raw reads are in /mnt/data/taxprofiler/input/reads/ on the Nextflow instance
    • the pipeline outputs used in R are in /data/workshop_data/ on the RStudio Server

    Reference databases

    All databases are pre-installed on the Nextflow instance under /mnt/data/taxprofiler/databases/ and /mnt/data/funcprofiler/databases/:

    • Kraken2 Standard-8 (k2_standard_08_GB_20260626)
    • MetaPhlAn mpa_vJun23_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202403
    • mOTUs v3.1.0
    • sylph GTDB r220 (gtdb_r220_c200)
    • HUMAnN 4 databases
    • eggNOG 5.0.2

    The lesson uses R 4.6 and Bioconductor 3.23. To reproduce the R episodes on your own computer, install R and RStudio Desktop, then run:

    R 

    install.packages(c("readr", "dplyr", "tidyr", "ggplot2", "BiocManager"))
BiocManager::install(version = "3.23")
BiocManager::install(c("SummarizedExperiment", "TreeSummarizedExperiment",
                       "mia", "miaViz"))

    You will also need a copy of the pipeline outputs. Change data_dir in the R episodes to the folder where you saved them.
